correctness.rationale: Writing B_{ki}=1{parent(k)=i} and X_j=1{j has no children}, each pair of different arrivals is independent. The only nonzero terms in Cov(B_{ki},X_j) are j=i (negative −w_i p_i/W_{k−1}) and 2≤j<k,j≠i (positive w_i w_j p_j/[W_{k−1}(W_{k−1}−w_j)]). Summation proves formula (1) for every n and positive real weight vector. For i=n−1, conditioning on the last parent choice proves a strict negative covariance with leaves since the root is not a leaf. The last vertex has D_n=0. Independent exhaustive enumeration of 24 possible increasing-parent maps at n=5 with exact rational product probabilities reproduces covariances (−2087/31104,25/10368,−1225/6912), and independently reproduces formula (1). For n<5 there are fewer than three nontrivial nonroot degree indices, so the alternating triple cannot occur; continuity preserves the sign pattern in an open increasing-weight neighbourhood.

value.rationale: The equal-weight chronological one-threshold sign rule naturally invites a robustness question under increasing fitness. The exact counterexample at the smallest possible order disproves that tempting extrapolation, and the universal formula allows diagnosis for arbitrary positive attachment profiles. A sharp motivated boundary is useful even without all-sign-pattern classification.

final_claim: For arbitrary positive deterministic weighted recursive-tree attachment, an exact labelled child-degree/leaf-count covariance identity holds; the penultimate vertex always has negative covariance, but strictly increasing weights (1,2,6,7,8) at minimal n=5 yield −,+,− covariance signs.
